notes.title: _sphinx_ext/_sphinx_ai_assistant: text files read or written without an explicit encoding (21 places)
notes.summary: In the AI assistant's documentation proxy, 21 calls open, read or write a text file without `encoding=`. Python then uses the locale's encoding: UTF-8 on most Linux and macOS systems, cp1252 or another code page on Windows and in some containers.
notes.why: The same file reads differently on two machines: non-ASCII text (names, accents, symbols) becomes mojibake or raises `UnicodeDecodeError` on Windows, and a file written there cannot be read back on Linux. Python 3.15 makes UTF-8 mode the default, which changes these calls' behaviour once more.
evidence: `scikitplot/_externals/_sphinx_ext/_sphinx_ai_assistant/_hf_spaces_proxy/security/promote_release.py:382`: `with path.open("rb") as src, zf.open(info, "w", force_zip64=False) as dst:`
notes.cause: Each call relies on `locale.getpreferredencoding()`; nothing states which encoding the file is in.
notes.expected: Every text-mode open, `read_text` and `write_text` names its encoding (`utf-8`, or `utf-8-sig` when a byte-order mark may be present), and a decode error says which file and encoding failed.
notes.constraints: Files the package writes are UTF-8 from now on; files a user hands in keep their own encoding rules (readers that detect encodings are not changed here).
edges: A path or content with non-ASCII characters on Windows (cp1252) and on a C/POSIX locale
A file with a UTF-8 byte-order mark
A file written by an older release in the locale encoding
notes.direction: Add `encoding="utf-8"` to each call; enable ruff's `PLW1514` (unspecified-encoding) for the area so new calls are caught; then `sweep_static.py --fail-on open-without-encoding` stays at zero for it.
accept: `sweep_static.py --list open-without-encoding` and `--list path-text-without-encoding` print nothing for the area
The area's tests pass under `PYTHONUTF8=0 LC_ALL=C` and on Windows CI

notes.title: _lib: library code prints to standard output instead of logging (28 calls)
notes.summary: 28 `print()` calls inside functions of GPU availability checks and helpers write directly to standard output.
notes.why: A caller cannot silence, redirect or level-filter `print`; it corrupts output that is meant to be parsed (a CLI's JSON, a notebook cell's result, an MCP server's stdio transport) and bypasses `scikitplot.logging`, which every other submodule uses.
evidence: `scikitplot/_lib/_array_api.py:1006`: `print("No GPUs available for CuPy. Required GPU.")`
`scikitplot/_lib/_array_api.py:1030`: `print("No GPUs available for TensorFlow. Using CPU.")`
`scikitplot/_lib/_array_api.py:1062`: `print("No GPUs available for JAX. Using CPU.")`
`scikitplot/_lib/_array_api.py:1090`: `print("No GPUs available for PyTorch. Using CPU.")`
notes.cause: Messages written for interactive use were never moved to the package's logger.
notes.expected: Library functions log through `logging.getLogger(__name__)` (or return the text); only command-line entry points print, and they print to the stream the command documents.
notes.constraints: Output a user relies on (a returned report) stays available, as a return value or an explicit `verbose`/`file=` argument.
edges: An MCP stdio server importing the area (stdout must carry only protocol messages)
Notebook use with logging unconfigured (the message must still be reachable)
notes.direction: Replace `print` with the module logger at the right level, or return the information; add ruff `T201` for the area's library modules.
accept: `sweep_static.py --list print-in-library` prints nothing unacknowledged for the area
A test captures stdout of the public functions and finds it empty

notes.title: _utils: broad exception handlers that do nothing (5 places)

notes.title: Runtime code uses Python 3.9 and 3.10 features while requires-python is >=3.8 (46 places)
notes.summary: `pyproject.toml` declares `requires-python = ">=3.8"`, but 46 places in first-party code need 3.9 or 3.10 at run time: `isinstance(x, A | B)`, `zip(strict=)`, `str.removeprefix`, and annotations evaluated at definition time that use `list[...]` or `X | Y`. 16 of them still need 3.10 when the floor is 3.9.
notes.why: A user on 3.8 or 3.9 can install the package and fail at import or first call with `TypeError` or `AttributeError`; the declared floor is a claim (Rule 5) that the code does not keep. This is the evidence for the open decision on the root `requires-python` (handoff backlog item 4).
evidence: `python -B tools/maint_tools/sweep_static.py --floor 3.8 --list <category>` for the four floor categories (main cba9383):
`scikitplot/_lib/doccer.py:31`: `def docformat(docstring: str, docdict: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> str:`
`scikitplot/experimental/_doremi/note.py:250`: `def sheet_to_note(sheet: Union[str, list, dict]) -> list[tuple[str, int, float]]:`
`--floor 3.9`: 16 findings remain (all `X | Y` unions, which need 3.10).
notes.cause: Code is tested on 3.10+ only; nothing runs the package on its declared floor.
notes.expected: Either the floor is raised to the lowest version the code runs on (3.10, with the locks and Pipenv store that already resolve only 3.10+), or the listed places are rewritten for 3.8 and a 3.8 test job proves it.
notes.constraints: Raising the floor is a public change (maintainer decision); rewriting keeps the floor but must be tested on 3.8 (Rule 137).

Partial distributions under `libs/` with their own floors
Vendored code with its own floor

accept: `sweep_static.py --floor <declared floor>` reports no floor finding
The test suite runs in CI on the declared floor

notes.title: _decorates: singleton load unpickles a file with no trust guard
notes.summary: `_decorates/_decorate.py` loads a singleton instance with `joblib.load(filename, ...)`, which unpickles the file: loading runs any code the file contains. Nothing asks whether the file is trusted.
notes.why: `scikitplot.corpus.load_documents` refuses pickle and joblib files unless `trusted=True` and checks an optional SHA-256 first (CORPUS-SEC-001); the same risk elsewhere in the package has no such guard, so the protection depends on which submodule a user calls.
notes.cause: Two submodules implemented deserialisation independently; the guard was never shared.
notes.expected: One shared guard: pickle-based loading requires an explicit `trusted=True` (or a matching SHA-256), and the error message says why.
notes.constraints: No change for callers that load their own trusted files once they pass `trusted=True`.
edges: A file that is not a pickle

notes.title: A base install cannot import the plotting API: the vendored seaborn copy imports seaborn
notes.summary: On `pip install scikit-plots` (no extras), the README quick start `sp.metrics.plot_precision_recall(...)` fails with `AttributeError: Module 'scikitplot' has no attribute 'metrics'. No module named 'seaborn'`. `scikitplot.api`, `decile`, `seaborn` and `visualkeras` all fail to import.
notes.why: The package's main feature does not work after the install the README tells users to run; the error does not say which extra to install.
evidence: Clean virtual environment, `pip install` of main (13b457d, CPython 3.13), no extras: the quick start raises the error above.
Traceback: `scikitplot/_compat/__init__.py` line 18 imports `scikitplot/externals/_seaborn`, whose `utils.py` line 17 runs `from seaborn._core.typing import deprecated` (the real seaborn).
`pyproject.toml` lists `seaborn` only in the `core` and `usage-skills` extras.
notes.cause: The vendored `_seaborn` package is not self-contained: it imports seaborn itself, and `_compat` imports it eagerly.
notes.expected: A base install imports `scikitplot.api` and runs the README quick start; or the README installs the extra and the error names it (`pip install "scikit-plots[core]"`).
notes.constraints: Choose one: make the vendored copy self-contained, declare seaborn as a base dependency, or require the extra explicitly; the README must match.
notes.direction: Recommended: remove the real-seaborn imports from the vendored copy (or import it lazily where only seaborn functions need it); add a CI job that runs the README quick start on a base install.
accept: A base install runs the README quick start
`sweep_runtime.py` reports no import error for `api`, `decile`, `seaborn`, `visualkeras` on a base install

notes.title: corpus: TextReader silently decodes legacy encodings as Latin-1 (CX-54)
notes.summary: `TextReader` reads files in cp1254 (Turkish), Shift-JIS and GB18030 as mojibake without a warning; only UTF-8 and BOM-marked UTF-16 come out right.
notes.why: Legacy encodings are common in government, academic and East Asian archives; mojibake is indexed and embedded as if it were text, and searches never match.
evidence: Probe (main cba9383): Turkish cp1254 `Iğdır'da şöyle bir çay içtik` reads as `Iðdýr'da þöyle bir çay içtik`.
Shift-JIS `日本語のテキスト...` reads as `\x93ú\x96{\x8cê...`; GB18030 `这是一个中文...` reads as `ÕâÊÇÒ»¸ö...`.
notes.cause: When strict UTF-8 fails, the reader falls back to a single-byte decoding instead of detecting the encoding or reporting the failure.
notes.expected: Encoding chosen by: an explicit `encoding=` argument, a BOM, strict UTF-8, then a detector (optional `charset-normalizer`) with a confidence threshold; below it, a warning naming the file and the chosen encoding.
notes.constraints: Same text for every UTF-8 file; detection deterministic.
edges: cp1252 vs Latin-1 vs cp1254 (Turkish letters)
notes.direction: Add a detection step and an `encoding` parameter; record the encoding in chunk metadata (already present as `encoding`).
accept: The four probe files read correctly with the detector installed; without it a warning names the fallback
Reader snapshot: no change for UTF-8 files

notes.cause: Tokenisation is left to the caller; the documented examples lower-case with `str.lower`.
notes.expected: A default analyzer that applies NFKC and `casefold`, with language-aware folding (`tr`, `az`: `İ`→`i`, `I`→`ı`) when `Analyzer(language=...)` says so; documented examples use it.
affected: the corpus keyword index that builds on it
notes.constraints: Scores for already-folded ASCII corpora unchanged.
notes.direction: Implement folding in `Analyzer`, use it when no tokenizer is given, and add the examples above as tests.
accept: The probe query scores the two Istanbul documents above zero

notes.expected: A scheduled and pull-request job that runs a vulnerability audit on the uv locks and requirements, and a release step that writes a CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM next to the wheels.
notes.constraints: Optional extra, imported lazily; no new base dependency; the same size, time and expansion limits as the existing readers and sources; no network access unless the caller asks for it; the licence of every library and model checked before it becomes a default; deterministic output for the same input and settings.
edges: Vulnerabilities without a fixed version (reported, not failing)
notes.direction: Use maintained, pinned actions; zizmor and action-validator clean.
accept: The job reports on every lock; the release includes an SBOM

probes.text: `grep -rln -E 'pip-audit|osv-scanner|cyclonedx|sbom' .github/workflows` finds nothing; `attest` appears only in `ci_docker_image_builder.yml` and the Docker registry workflows (main cba9383).
